newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rheinmetall takes over Badenwerk units.
newsitem.headline: Rheinmetall takes over Badenwerk units.

text.p: German defence and electronics group Rheinmetall AG said on Wednesday it would take management control of Badenwerk Holding AG's electronics business via a share swap between the two partners' subsidiaries.
Under the deal, utility Badenwerk will sell 75.5 percent of Kommunikations Industrie Holding and all of Kreutler GmbH to Rheinmetall Elektronik AG, a unit of Rheinmetall.

Badenwerk in return will receive 12.5 percent of Rheinmetall Elektronik, with an option to raise its stake to a qualified minority shareholding of 25 percent plus one share, Rheinmetall said in a regulatory news release.
No financial details of the transaction were published.

Rheinmetall said the deal, which awaits approval from the German cartel office, marked a logical step forward after the two companies teamed up last year to buy a controlling stake in defence electronics group STN Atlas Elektronik.
The takeover will also increase turnover at Rheinmetall Elektronik by around 250 million marks a year to 1.2 billion marks. The division will employ around 5,900 workers.

Rheinmetall has pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy over the past year to lessen its dependence on its core defence business, which has been squeezed by military budget cuts. It recently snapped up auto parts supplier Kolbenschmidt after a long takeover tussle with Britain's T&N.

Rheinmetall's shares have climbed sharply on the back of the acquisitions, and were up 3.50 marks at 410 marks in morning trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange, compared to below 200 marks in late 1996.
